priorRegression.sameDeckTest: Failed headed WebKit at line 550: document scroll 200 became element scroll 0 after Deck entry; retained outer DOM and 390 px width assertions passed. No retry.
priorRegression.diagnostic: Separate delegated-write trace confirmed a document scroll event at 200 and element handoff write 200 landing at 200 before a later restoration write 0. This diagnostic did not establish a unique route-adapter cause; an independent Chromium export without the adapter also failed.
priorRegression.correction: Owner handoffs remain available until the receiving restorer consumes them, or owner/content lifetime ends. Token-scoped release protects newer transfers; pending user input can update the intended offset. No arbitrary time delay.

inputReliability.deckSetup: The final source test uses wheel input and scroll-event barriers for document offset 200 before entry and element offset 300 before exit. Existing offset, width, DOM-retention and return assertions are unchanged. The other six cases are unchanged.
inputReliability.why: Separate bounded Chromium diagnostics showed the earlier synchronous scrollTo(200) plus immediate DOM click could toggle before any source 200 scroll event. Waiting only for numeric scrollY=200 was insufficient to establish the observer-owned reading position.
inputReliability.interpretation: This test-input correction is separate from the delayed restoration lifetime bug: the prior failing WebKit diagnostic did observe source 200 and an element handoff write landing 200 before restoration later reset. A no-adapter control with reliable wheel input passed and does not discriminate the lifetime correction.

finalDeckInputVerification.sequence: After the seven-test run below, only the Deck exit setup changed to a wheel toward element offset300 with a matching scroll-event barrier. The other six source files/test cases and runtime export stayed unchanged. The final Deck test alone was rerun and passed.
